historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Management FY26 guidance (~5% reported / ~3.5% underlying), backlog +7% ($8.2B) and underlying orders +7% in Q3 FY26, and the mid-single-digit through-cycle organic target. Historical CAGRs are not usable as the anchor: revenue 5yr 1.4% spans the Copeland/InSinkErator exits; 3yr 9.3% embeds the NI acquisition; equity 5yr 19.2% is the FY23 Copeland gain; FY23 owner FCF was ~$0 on divestiture tax payments.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 19.2% vs revenue 5yr 1.4% and EPS 5yr 4.5%: divergence >30% - driven by the FY2023 $13.2B net income (Copeland gain) rather than by operating compounding. Flagged; equity CAGR not used.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF = reported FCF - SBC (interest income not stripped: net debt company). Series (USD m): FY20 2,435; FY21 2,947; FY22 2,479; FY23 3 (OCF hit by divestiture taxes); FY24 2,653; FY25 2,404 total basis / 2,982 continuing basis (FY25 total OCF includes -$578M discontinued-ops tax on the Copeland stake sale); FY26E 3,350. SBC-adjusted CAGRs sit ~1-2pp below reported because SBC rose from $110M (FY20) to $263M (FY25) with the NI/AspenTech software workforce - SBC is growing faster than cash flow, though at 1.3-1.5% of revenue it is small in absolute terms.

scenario_narratives.base: Emerson is now a ~40%-software process-automation company with a record $8.2B backlog. Base assumes the power/grid, LNG and semiconductor cycles deliver 5-5.5% growth for two years, fading to 2.5% by FY36, while software mix and NI/AspenTech synergies add ~30bp/yr of EBITDA margin to 30.5%. The Middle East logistics headwind (~$100M FY26) and China weakness (-3%) roll off but are not reversed. Non-deductible acquisition amortization is left out of the build (no cash, no shield). Buybacks fund a flat share count; net debt of $10.9B (1.9x EBITDA) is deducted once. The axes that matter are (1) whether the growth-vertical orders (+27%) convert to shipped revenue at software-like margins, and (2) whether the hardware half (Intelligent Devices, 55% of sales) stays above trough through the next capex cycle.
scenario_narratives.bull: The AI/data-centre power buildout (1.7 GW award, Ovation +31%), the LNG funnel ($2.2B) and the semiconductor T&M recovery (+70% orders) run concurrently for 3-4 years, lifting growth to 7-7.5% and pulling AspenTech/DeltaV software to 40%+ of revenue. Company EBITDA reaches 32% - a level no automation peer has achieved, which is why this is the bull and not the base. A Safety & Productivity sale at a full multiple would be upside on top (not modelled). Terminal growth 3.0%, cap 20x.
scenario_narratives.bear: A FY28 industrial-capex recession (oil/chemicals overcapacity, tariff retaliation, financing-cost-driven project deferrals) coincides with China staying weak and the Strait of Hormuz disruption persisting. Revenue falls 3% at the trough, EBITDA deleverages to 26%, and the recovery is muted because software growth stalls at the current ACV and NI synergies disappoint. Leverage at 1.9x means no solvency risk, but $4B of commercial paper must be termed out at higher coupons. Terminal growth 2.0%, cap 15x. The bear does not hit the zero floor - the business remains a ~$3B FCF generator throughout.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF DCF, SBC fully expensed, share count flat and funded by buybacks, net debt of $10.9B deducted once at the 2026-06-30 balance sheet. The build is unlevered and uses only cash-tax-deductible D&A so the ~$1.1B/yr of non-deductible acquired-intangible amortization creates neither a phantom tax shield nor a fake cost. The market pays ~27x EV/FCF and ~22x forward P/E for Emerson's software re-rating; at an 8.5% WACC the house basis says that price already embeds the bull case. The stock is a quality compounder that is not cheap.
key_risks_to_valuation: Terminal value carries most of the EV: a 1pp move in WACC or terminal growth swings value ~15-20% (see sensitivity grid).
FY0 is guidance-based (FY26 ends 2026-09-30, reports ~mid-Nov 2026): replace with actuals at the next update; the FY26 FCF print vs $3.6B guide is the first checkpoint.
EBITDA margin is derived from GAAP pretax + interest + D&A, not a company-reported total-company EBITDA; a ~1pp error in the FY26E starting margin is ~$8/share.

The cash tax rate treatment (22% on EBIT after deductible D&A only) is a judgment on how much of the $1.1B amortization is deductible; if more is deductible than assumed, value is understated by up to ~$5/share.
Safety & Productivity divestiture (~8% of revenue) is not modelled; a sale below fair value or a prolonged process would be dilutive.
~$4B of commercial paper from the AspenTech buyout is short-dated; a refinancing at 5%+ raises interest (outside the unlevered build but a real equity cost).

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 122.64-166.35.
data_sources.financials: SEC XBRL companyfacts (CIK 32604): 10-Q Q3 FY2026 (period ended 2026-06-30) for cash, debt, shares, 9M cash flows, SBC, D&A, taxes; 10-K FY2025 for annual D&A split (depreciation $344M / amortization $1,174M), taxes paid $1,440M, interest paid $221M, operating lease cost $201M and liability $643M, continuing vs discontinued OCF ($3,676M / -$578M). EMR_Metrics.csv for the history pivot.
data_sources.qualitative: EMR_Analysis.json (2026-09-28): Q3 FY2026 results and raised FY26 guidance (sales ~+5%, adj EPS ~$6.55, FCF ~$3.6B, capital return ~$2.2B), backlog $8.2B, ACV $1.68B, Middle East headwind ~$100M, Safety & Productivity strategic review.

inputs.sbc_source: 10-Q Q3 FY2026 cash-flow add-back (ShareBasedCompensation) 9M $181M annualised to ~$250M; FY2025 10-K $263M, FY2024 $260M. Cash tax withholding on net-share settlement is not tagged separately by Emerson (nets inside other financing, -$134M 9M FY26 incl. other items) so the add-back is used unadjusted; no company combined figure exists.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 financing outflow $1,167M; 9M FY2026 $898M, FY26 guide ~$1.0B. The flat 560.1M count is funded: buybacks (~$1.0-1.2B/yr) exceed SBC (~$0.25B) roughly 4x, and the diluted count has fallen from 566.7M (FY25) to 561.1M (Q3 FY26).
inputs.fy0_basis: FY ends 30 Sep 2026, reports mid-Nov 2026. FY0 revenue = FY2025 actual $18,016M x guided ~5% reported growth = $18,900M (9M FY26 actual $13,781M, +4.7% YoY; Q3 +7.0%). FY0 reported FCF = FY26 guidance ~$3.6B (9M actual OCF $2,902M - capex $284M = $2,618M). Chosen over FY2025 actuals because the balance sheet is 2026-06-30: using FY25 as FY0 would count 9M of FY26 cash both in net debt and in year-1 flows. Q4 FY26 FCF (~$1.0B) accrues before the model's year 1 and is not credited - ~$1.8/share of conservatism.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-09-25T20:03:59Z regular close (Friday); valuation dated Monday 2026-09-28 pre-open
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 557.8M common shares outstanding at 2026-06-30 (10-Q cover / CommonStockSharesOutstanding) + 2.3M dilutive awards (Q3 FY26 diluted 561.1M less basic 558.8M weighted average) = 560.1M. Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows (charging both would double-count).
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Risk-free ~4.2% (10y UST), beta ~1.1, ERP ~4.5-5% -> cost of equity ~9.2%; pre-tax cost of debt ~4.5% (A2/A rated; legacy low-coupon bonds plus ~$4B CP), ~3.5% after tax; capital structure ~87% equity ($88.6B market cap) / 13% debt ($13.1B) -> WACC ~8.4-8.6%. 8.5% used in ALL scenarios: risk is carried in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked into per-scenario discount rates (adaptations item f).
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) leases as operating cost. US GAAP ASC 842 operating lease cost (~$201M FY25) is already inside EBITDA; operating lease liabilities ($643M at FY25) are therefore EXCLUDED from net debt. Finance leases are immaterial (no tag).
inputs.nci_treatment: None required. NCI fell from $5,873M (FY24, AspenTech 45% minority) to $15M at 2026-06-30 after the March 2025 buyout of the remaining AspenTech shares; NCI profit share was $0 in Q3 FY26. Flows are effectively 100% attributable.
inputs.da_treatment: da_pct_path is the CASH-TAX-DEDUCTIBLE D&A only: depreciation (~$350M, 1.9% of revenue) plus the deductible slice of amortization. Total GAAP D&A is ~$1,480M (7.8%) because ~$1.1B/yr of acquired-intangible amortization from the NI (FY24) and AspenTech stock deals is non-cash AND largely non-deductible (FY25 continuing cash taxes ~$860M vs $696M book expense; DTL unwinding $2,300M -> $1,696M over 9M FY26). A non-cash, non-deductible charge has zero FCF effect, so it is left out of the build rather than modelled with a phantom tax shield that would then be perpetuated in the terminal value. Cash tax rate (22%) is applied to EBIT after deductible D&A only. Deductible amortization fades from ~2.1% to ~1.1% of revenue as older layers roll off.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (routing row: operating company, cyclical industrial -> owner-fcf.md + adaptations for leases/NCI/cyclicality). First valuation of this ticker; no memory entry. Emerson is a going-concern operating company whose value is a stream of free cash flow; none of the non-FCF rows apply. EBITDA margin path is company-level adjusted EBITDA BEFORE SBC and AFTER restructuring (~$140-170M/yr, treated as recurring): FY26E ~29.0%, derived from 9M FY26 GAAP pretax $2,484M + Q4E ~$950M + net interest ~$345M + D&A ~$1,480M = ~$5.2B post-SBC / ~$5.5B pre-SBC; cross-checks against guided adjusted segment EBITA ~28% + segment depreciation ~1.9% - corporate ~1%. The engine's year-1 (FY27) unlevered owner FCF (~$3.85B) sits above the FY26 levered guidance ($3.6B) by after-tax net interest (~$270M) plus one year of growth, less SBC; that is expected for an EV-based build in which the $10.9B net debt is deducted separately. CSV caveat: the XBRL-derived quarterly rows in EMR_Metrics.csv are shifted one quarter (the 'Q2 2026' revenue row of $4,873M is Apr-Jun 2026 = Q3 FY26 per XBRL period dates); all anchors here use XBRL period dates. Safety & Productivity (~$1.4B sales, ~8% of revenue, under strategic review since Nov 2024) is NOT carved out: a sale at fair value is roughly value-neutral to the DCF and no buyer or price exists. Historical CAGRs are heavily distorted by the portfolio transformation (Copeland/InSinkErator divestitures FY21-23, NI acquisition FY24, AspenTech buyout FY25, Copeland gain in FY23 EPS/equity) and are reported but not used as the growth anchor.

bear.growth_rationale: An FY28 industrial-capex downturn (oil price / chemicals overcapacity / tariff-driven recession) on top of persistent China weakness: revenue -3% in FY28 (FY16-type trough was -10% on the old, more cyclical portfolio; software mix halves the beta). Recovery to ~3% and fade to 2%.
bear.margin_rationale: Volume deleverage takes company EBITDA to 26% at the FY28 trough (still above the FY25 level of ~27.5% minus one turn), then recovers only to 28% - the software mix shift stalls, NI integration synergies disappoint, and Pillar 2 lifts the cash tax rate to 23%.

base.growth_rationale: FY27-28 at 5.5%: backlog +7%, orders +7%, power/LNG/semis verticals +27% offset by China (-3%) and ~$100M Middle East logistics drag rolling off. Fades to 2.5% by FY36 as the LNG/power project cycle matures.
base.margin_rationale: FY26E ~29.0% pre-SBC company EBITDA (guided adj segment EBITA ~28% +140bp YoY). +30bp/yr from software mix (ACV +9%, S&S margin 31.8%) and NI/AspenTech synergies to 30.5% by FY33 - roughly the incremental-margin math on 5% growth, already ~5pp above Honeywell.
base.wc_rationale: Net trade working capital (receivables ~$3.0B + inventory ~$2.2B - payables ~$1.4B - deferred revenue ~$1.1B) is ~14% of revenue; FY24/FY25 operating-capital builds were $151M/$9M. Growth consumes ~12% of each year's revenue increase; sign negative per the manufacturer rule.

bull.growth_rationale: Top of the 4-7% organic band plus pricing: AI data-centre on-site power (1.7 GW award), Ovation orders +31% with lead times into 2028, LNG funnel $2.2B, semiconductor T&M orders +70% - all running concurrently for 3-4 years.
bull.margin_rationale: Software mix reaches ~40%+ of revenue with AspenTech pricing; company EBITDA to 32% (best-in-class, above any automation peer). Growth verticals carry higher incremental margins.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 18x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default is 15/50/35. Bear raised to 20% because four independent, currently live headwinds - Middle East logistics (quantified $100M), China (-3%), tariff policy flagged as material in the 10-K, and a hardware half still tied to oil/chemicals capex - make a mid-decade downturn a normal outcome for this business, not a tail. Bull trimmed to 30% because it needs three cycles (power, LNG, semis) to overlap AND margins to reach a level (32%) above every peer. No going-concern or single-customer risk, so bear is not pushed higher.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
